title: NeoMundi Evidence Gateway - response envelope, version 1
description: What the gateway returns. `engine_report` is the engine's own report, republished with local filesystem paths redacted; the gateway adds no control line, no count and no verdict of its own.

performs_verification.description: Always false, by construction. The gateway is a transport and an envelope, not a verifier.

status.description: `completed` means the engine ran and produced a machine report - it does NOT mean the artifact passed. Read `verdict` and `exit_code` for that.

verification_performed.description: A fact about this gateway run, not about the artifact: true only when the engine ran and its report was read. False on `rejected` and `engine_unavailable`.

sha256_reported_by_engine.description: Taken from the engine report. The gateway does not hash the artifact itself - doing so would be a second integrity implementation.

engine.description: What was reached, and under what declaration. `revision_declared` is declared by the operator and never verified here.

verdict.description: Null unless the engine ran. Every field is copied from the engine report.

engine_report.description: The engine's report, verbatim except for path redaction. Its own `schema` field names the contract it follows.

engine_report_redacted.description: True when at least one string in the engine report was rewritten to remove a local path. Stated rather than silent: a redacted report is no longer byte-identical to what the engine wrote.

limits.description: Always non-empty. Carries the gateway's own two limits, plus every `does_not_establish` line of the engine report.

exit_code.description: 0/1/2 are the engine's own codes, passed through untranslated. 3 = engine unavailable, 4 = request refused; both mean no verification took place.
